mission_title: Deldo import safety boundary: explicit data classification, enforced at run time
phase: Complete. Classification is enforced at run time at the import boundary and re-asserted at the persistence plan. Persistence remains gated.

source_authority.deldo: API documentation.pdf and 26933TEST.csv, supplied by Jan Van Dyck (Deldo NV), subject 'RE: Connect platform and orders for - 026933 (Go Rush Trasporti srl)'. Both inspected directly in this session. GoRush customer number 026933.
source_authority.note: The PDF does NOT document the CSV columns ('we send you 1 file in CSV format so that you can examine file header and structure'). The sample file IS the column contract, and every mapping was read off it.
source_authority.deldo_reverified: Both primary artefacts were re-read independently on 2026-09-22 and every PRIMARY claim in docs/suppliers/deldo/README.md was re-derived from them: 26933TEST.csv (1,322,596 bytes, sha256 5e384ccf45d06ec3..., 6,729 data rows, 35 columns, ';' delimited, no quoting, POINT decimal separator on 6729/6729 Price values, pure ASCII, LF endings, 0 malformed rows) and API documentation.pdf (18 pages). DOCUMENTATION ONLY. Recorded the approved commercial architecture decisions in docs/architecture/04_SALES_SOURCING_MODEL.md: supplier identity invisible to customers; customer buys only from GommaRush; standard up to ~7 days vs express ~24-48h manually sourced from the Italian supplier; the 15-20% express share recorded explicitly as a planning assumption and not a rule; supplier minimum quantities and consolidation supported internally; customer order acceptance and supplier purchase/release as separate events; many customer orders per supplier batch; delivery promises must account for consolidation and cut-off rather than raw supplier availability; normal/older-DOT/Demo kept distinguishable; older-DOT offerable as a clearly identified cheaper GommaRush option; supplied DOT year preserved; Deldo Demo meaning unverified and not to be inferred; exact supplier listing/article survives sourcing and ordering; V1 payments bank transfer, POS on delivery, cash; manual review of every customer order; customer-specific pricing supported architecturally; portal and WhatsApp on one catalogue/pricing/order engine.
Added Deldo activation question 8 (what does the Demo column mean), noting explicitly that no DOT-encoding question is needed because the feed already supplies the year.

risks: buildDeldoImport currently has NO non-test caller: there is no admin route, upload route or server action that reaches Deldo import. So there was no live bypass to close. The runtime guard was added because the FIRST such route - the next mission is feed activation - would otherwise pass unvalidated JSON straight through an erased TypeScript type.

guardKnownTestFile only recognises the one named file 26933TEST.csv. It is a deliberate backstop, not a heuristic, and must not be broadened into 'looks like test data' - such a guess would eventually be wrong in the expensive direction.

CORRECTED: a prior session working on the unrelated branch claude/sleepy-gauss-lezg26 concluded that no Deldo parser could be written because the primary files had never been inspected. That was wrong. The parser exists, is grounded in 26933TEST.csv, and is tested. That branch diverged from d6e2cda and never contained any of this Deldo work; it duplicated the schema baseline independently. Do not merge it over this branch.

Discount range was misstated as '-407.69 to +63.23' in both src/lib/suppliers/deldo/feed/parse.ts and docs/DELDO_ACTIVATION.md. The true range across 3,639 non-zero values is -407.69 to +78.33; 644 rows exceeded the stated upper bound. Both corrected. The conclusion drawn from it - never apply Discount - was and remains correct.

Stock in 26933TEST.csv has a hard floor of 3 and a hard ceiling of 100 (464 rows at exactly 100, none above, no zero-stock rows). That looks like deliberate banding rather than true counts, so it must not be presented as an exact quantity until Deldo confirms the semantics.

risks.summary: Production's function bodies were not created from the repository's migrations: 12 of 28 have their comments stripped and differ in formatting, though all 28 are semantically identical.
risks.impact: Evidence that functions too were applied outside version control. No behavioural difference exists today, but the same practice produced R15.
risks.resolution: The baseline carries the repository's commented versions. Requiring all schema change to go through migrations, enforced by the verify script in CI, is the fix.

risks.summary: RESOLVED IN SOURCE, NOT YET IN THE LEDGER. The 14 tables that no migration created are now in supabase/baseline/, proved to rebuild from empty. What remains is reconciling production's migration ledger, which needs a backup and approval (B9).
risks.impact: Until the ledger is reconciled, `supabase db push` against production is still unpredictable. The schema itself is no longer at risk of being lost.

risks.summary: Production changes were historically applied outside the migration system. A captured baseline fixes the past but not the practice.
risks.impact: Without a rule and a check, the divergence recurs and the next baseline is needed in months.
risks.resolution: scripts/verify-migration-baseline.sh is now CI-suitable and asserts every object count. Wiring it into CI closes this.

risks.summary: Deldo documentation conflicts with itself on the GET_STOCK request parameter. The 'URL Parameters' section lists productId=[integer|string] OR ean=[string]; both worked examples use article=.
risks.impact: A wrong parameter name means every live lookup fails, or worse, silently returns nothing useful.
risks.resolution: article= is implemented because it is the only form demonstrated. Confirm with Deldo when requesting the token - it costs one line in the same email as B5.

risks.summary: The Discount column's meaning is undocumented and values range from -407.69 to +63.23. A plain percentage discount cannot be negative.
risks.impact: If Discount must be applied to reach the real purchase price, every Deldo cost is currently wrong. If it must not, applying it later would corrupt every margin.
risks.resolution: Carried verbatim and never applied. purchasePrice is the Price column as supplied. Needs D7.

risks.summary: Which of Deldo's two documented pricing modes GoRush receives is not stated anywhere - tyre price with transport separate, or transport included for a destination country.
risks.impact: The same number means different things under each. A markup applied to the wrong interpretation misprices every Deldo tyre.
risks.resolution: Every observation carries commercialMode 'unknown', which classifyObservation treats as not commercially usable. Needs D8.

risks.summary: Neither the feed nor the API returns a currency.
risks.impact: Deldo is Belgian and EUR is the obvious assumption, but an assumed currency on a purchase price is exactly the class of silent error this integration must not make.
risks.resolution: currency is left null. Needs D8 alongside the pricing mode.

risks.summary: 530 of 6,729 rows are flagged for review: 459 parenthesised or damaged load/speed values, 70 three-digit truck rims, 3 imperial widths.
risks.impact: Descriptive only - no commercial field is affected. These rows import with null dimensions rather than guesses.
risks.resolution: Acceptable. Revisit if search quality suffers.
